hook: A Keter file about a cargo ship that vanished in 1998 and turned up adrift off a Japanese island in 2015, at the center of a zone where physics no longer behaves. It is long and built mostly from inquiry testimony, so its real subject emerges gradually from people contradicting one another. Content note: one survivor describes in graphic detail what happened to bodies inside the zone, and the testimonies are full of profanity.
whyItMatters:
Inside this article, Scranton Reality Anchors are praised by their defenders as proven, everyday safety equipment used all over the Foundation, and the file's move is to put that trusted hardware in the dock. It is structured like an accident investigation, complete with a contractor, a consultant, a skeptic, a stubborn director and the crew who refused his orders.

The bureaucracy tag fits: the anomaly matters less than the way an institution talks itself into trusting a product.
thingsToNotice:
The answer arrives in the leaked 1995 email: anchor failures were climbing everywhere, each failing unit needed two clean ones to hold it back, and the engineer said the ship needed fifteen to eighteen, yet DeVorn's company installed six. The devices meant to suppress reality-benders produced the warped zone, and Browning's plan to push into it shielded by more anchors made things worse: Asakawa, the young technician, turned partly to glass and took twenty minutes to shatter and bleed out, Sanchez turned inside out, Browning's bones seemed to evaporate, and Voccola lost three limbs.

Sivori's tiger speech in the 1999 inquiry reads as plain foreshadowing once you know this. Bakshi's testimony is the emotional center, because he could have pulled Asakawa off the boat and stayed silent out of a wish to see Browning punished. The coda flips the tone entirely: O5-5, calling herself an old monster left over from a crueler Foundation, has caught the escaped DeVorn, left him a jumpsuit and his own newest anchor in a cell, and invites him to give it a test run.
